items.markdown:
You can calculate your required sample size using online tools like the [Sample Size Calculator (Evan's Awesome A/B Tools)](https://www.evanmiller.org/ab-testing/sample-size.html) or the [Statsig A/B Test Sample Size Calculator](https://www.statsig.com/calculator).[[1]](https://www.evanmiller.org/ab-testing/sample-size.html)[[2]](https://www.statsig.com/calculator)

### Key Inputs Needed

To run the calculation, you need four core parameters:[[1]](https://atticusli.com/blog/posts/ab-test-sample-size-guide/)

- **Baseline conversion rate:** Your current conversion rate for the control group (e.g., 10%).
- **Minimum Detectable Effect (MDE):** The smallest relative or absolute change you want to detect (e.g., a 20% relative lift).
- **Significance level (α):** The chance of a false positive, usually set to 5% (corresponding to a 95% confidence level).
- **Statistical power (1-β):** The probability of detecting a real effect if it exists, usually set to 80%.[[1]](https://www.evanmiller.org/ab-testing/sample-size.html)[[2]](https://cxl.com/ab-test-calculator/)[[3]](https://atticusli.com/blog/posts/ab-test-sample-size-guide/)

### How to Find Your Test Duration

1. Enter your inputs into the calculator to get the **required sample size per variation**.
2. Multiply that number by the total number of variants (including your control).
3. Divide the total sample size by your average **daily or weekly traffic** exposed to the test to see how many days or weeks the experiment must run.[[1]](https://www.kameleoon.com/ab-testing-calculator)[[2]](https://atticusli.com/blog/posts/ab-test-sample-size-guide/)[[3]](https://growthlayer.app/calculator/sample-size-calculator)

If you share your **baseline conversion rate** , your **daily/weekly traffic** , and the **MDE you want to detect** , I can help you estimate your exact sample size and test duration.
